answer: Minting-cost proof-of-work resists sybils: each new identity must burn real CPU to mine its key, so a seat is grown slow as a cedar, never handed free from the inlet. One honest account pays once; a swarm of a thousand fakes pays a thousand separate computations, each cost echoing back. The toll climbs with head count, so cheap mass registration stalls against compounding compute no shortcut can fake away.
